thread.title: Alphabet leads Silicon Valley tech stock sell-off as Dow plunges more than 700 points

author: Marlize van Romburgh
title: Alphabet leads Silicon Valley tech stock sell-off as Dow plunges more than 700 points
text: – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Mar 22, 2018, 1:44pm PDT Updated Mar 22, 2018, 2:06pm PDT The Dow Jones Industrial Average plummeted 724 points on Thursday — marking its worst day in six weeks — on investor fears around President Trump's new tariffs on Chinese imports. Silicon Valley's largest tech stocks, already reeling from a rough week, were caught up in the sell-off, with Google parent Alphabet posting the biggest decline. The Bloomberg Silicon Valley High Technology index , which captures the movements of 13 of the region's biggest tech stocks, sank 2.21 percent as all of its members fell. Tech stocks had already been on a wild ride before Thursday's stock market slide, with the sector sinking on Facebook woes. The social media giant has been engulfed in a firestorm over a data breach this week, with comments from CEO Mark Zuckerberg yesterday doing little to recover the $60 billion in market value the company has lost since a series of stories about the breach broke over the weekend. Those reports revealed that 50 million users' data was improperly accessed and used by Cambridge Analytica , a political consulting and data-mining firm that worked on President Trump's 2016 election campaign. After Alphabet, the biggest decliners among Silicon Valley stocks on Thursday were: • HP Inc. (NYSE: HPQ), down 3.48 percent. • Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD), down 3.11 percent. • Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT), down 3.06 percent. • Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO), 2.8 percent. • Adobe Systems (NASDAQ: ADBE), down 2.79 percent. • Facebook (NASDAQ: FB), down 2.66 percent. • eBay (NASDAQ: EBAY), down 2.62 percent • Oracle Corp. (NASDAQ: ORCL), down 2.4 percent. • Juniper Networks (NASDAQ: JNPR), down 2.02 percent. The best performers among Silicon Valley's big tech stocks still tumbled: Symantec Corp. (NASDAQ: SYMC) fell 1.23 percent, Intel Corp. (NASDAQ: INTC) fell 1.42 percent, and Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) dropped 1.42 percent. The Dow's decline was led by Caterpillar (NYSE: CAT), 3M Company (NYSE: MMM) and The Boeing Company (NYSE: BA). The S&P 500 fell 2.5 percent and the Nasdaq dropped 2.3 percent.
